blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — cholestyramine drug interactions and timing
stem: A client takes cholestyramine for hyperlipidemia and several other oral medications. Which instruction should the nurse provide?

options.A: Take other oral medications at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after cholestyramine because the resin can bind drugs in the gastrointestinal tract and reduce absorption.
options.B: Take the other oral medications together with cholestyramine because concurrent administration improves absorption and prevents clinically important gastrointestinal drug binding.
options.C: Switch cholestyramine to a subcutaneous injection when other oral medications are prescribed because the oral resin cannot be separated safely from concomitant drug therapy.
options.D: Medication timing does not matter because cholestyramine is systemically absorbed before it can bind other drugs or interfere with their gastrointestinal absorption.

rationale: Current cholestyramine labeling states that the resin may bind concurrently administered oral drugs and delay or reduce their absorption. The label recommends taking other drugs at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after cholestyramine, or at as great an interval as possible. Cholestyramine acts in the gastrointestinal tract rather than requiring systemic absorption. Therefore A is correct. B and D contradict the labeled interaction, and C misstates the route of administration.
educational_objective: Teach clients taking cholestyramine to separate other oral medications by at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after the resin because gastrointestinal drug binding can reduce absorption.
source_document_title: CHOLESTYRAMINE for Oral Suspension USP — Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label section dated June 15, 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Drug Interactions: cholestyramine may delay or reduce absorption of concomitant oral medications; because it may bind other drugs, take other drugs at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after cholestyramine, or at as great an interval as possible.
source_claim_supported: Cholestyramine can bind concomitant oral drugs and reduce their absorption; current labeling recommends separation by at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after the resin.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four options as complete medication-timing or administration statements of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the June 2026 cholestyramine labeling. No absolute cue or second defensible timing instruction remains.
